title: Duplex AEAD Birthday-Term Tightness and Capacity Sizing
summary: Existing bounds with unrestricted forgery data complexity contain a birthday term; whether it is proof-induced and whether duplex capacity can safely be well below twice the target security level remain open.

formal_statement.body: Is the $\sigma_d^2$ birthday term an artifact of the proofs, and can $c$ be dimensioned safely below $2s$?

scope.domain: Security bounds and parameter sizing for duplex-based AEAD constructions.
assumptions: The forgery data complexity $\sigma_d$ is unrestricted.
parameters: $\sigma_d$: forgery data complexity whose square appears as the birthday term
$c$: capacity value of the duplex construction
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the squared forgery-data birthday term is a proof artifact and whether capacity can safely be dimensioned well below twice the targeted security level.

citations.label: Generic Attack on Duplex-Based AEAD Modes using Random Function Statistics

progress.summary: The paper presents its generic attack as a step toward determining the exact security of duplex-based constructions. It explicitly leaves the birthday-term tightness and safe capacity sizing unresolved.
citation_labels: Henri Gilbert et al., Generic Attack on Duplex-Based AEAD Modes using Random Function Statistics
